intro.title: Concurrent Mode Gotchas
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple React app to understand common pitfalls when using Concurrent Mode. You'll learn how Concurrent Mode can cause unexpected behavior in components that rely on synchronous state updates or external data. The core concepts covered include state management, side effects, and React's rendering lifecycle. You'll use React hooks like useState and useEffect, and work with JSX to create the user interface. This hands-on exercise will help you write more predictable and efficient React applications.
intro.usecase: Concurrent Mode is crucial for building responsive, high-performance applications like live dashboards, real-time collaboration tools, or complex e-commerce product filters. For example, when a user interacts with a large data table—sorting columns while new data streams in—Concurrent Mode ensures the UI remains interactive, preventing janky rendering or input lag. Developers implementing features such as background data fetching during route transitions or prioritizing urgent UI updates (like a typing indicator) over less critical ones rely on these patterns to deliver a seamless user experience.
